output.brief:
The failures come from Pellacott's 2026 valves, not installers or firmware. Brenmoor's lab found 11% of never-installed 2026 Pellacott valves leaking at the seat, versus 1% of 2025 Pellacott and none of Durrant-Hale valves. Pellacott valves fail at about 40 per 1,000 whichever installers or firmware they meet; Durrant-Hale's sit at 5–7. New firms look worse only because they mostly fit 2026-built units.

Pellacott's score rose because its paperwork became complete, but the records don't reflect real tests: an independent contractor found the leak rig out of service since 9 January, no other test equipment, and certificates repeating the same four sets of numbers. Fresh certificates would prove nothing.

Do now: keep the six lots held, quarantine all 2026 Pellacott stock, withdraw dock-to-stock, release only valves passing Brenmoor's own helium test, and ask Durrant-Hale for extra supply. Drop the installer plan and chargebacks. Then require rig logs or witnessed tests for score credit, spot-check other suppliers, and test whether the seal or the new line is at fault.

Confident on cause and containment; unsure on seal-versus-line and other suppliers.
